transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-05 15:30 PST | Duration 62m | Attendees: Sofia M. (Redwood AE), Ethan P. (Redwood SE), Priya N. (Lyra CTO), Marcus H. (Platform), Asha S. (Lead ML)

00:00 Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, how's it going?
00:04 Priya Nair: good, thanks — excited to dig in, quick context: we're building an embeddable ai-assistant across our product lines, want to lock in infra choices early.
00:12 Sofia Martinez: awesome, Ethan will lead the integration bits, i'll cover pricing and deployment options.
00:18 Ethan Park: cool, quick agenda: sdk examples, langchain/llamaindex connectors, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limiting & quotas, observability hooks, and then q&a. Sound good?
00:26 Priya Nair: yep.

02:05 Ethan Park: first, SDKs — Redwood has JS and Python SDKs, plus a low-level HTTP REST endpoint. We also have streaming clients for server-sent events and websocket patterns. How are you planning to call the model today?
02:16 Asha Singh: currently we proxy calls through our internal gateway to openai, using a very thin wrapper. We do batching at the edge for chat history and call embeddings as a separate async pipeline. We prefer a unified approach if possible.
02:30 Marcus Holt: one ask is that we keep per-customer rate-limits; we have multi-tenant routing and need to make sure a sudden spike from one customer doesn't blow up costs.
02:42 Ethan Park: understood — you can use Redwood's API key per-tenant pattern, or put a Redwood gateway in front of your gateway. Two approaches: one, your app directly calls Redwood SDK and we handle routing; two, you keep a proxy/gateway that multiplexes to Redwood and enforce your own per-customer quotas.
02:58 Priya Nair: can you expand on the gateway option? we worry about double-hop latency.

05:15 Ethan Park: sure — the proxy approach means you vended a single internal endpoint. Your gateway will do authentication, tenant mapping, and local caching. Then the gateway talks to Redwood. The benefit is centralized observability and local quota enforcement. Cost is added network hop and complexity. With batching/prefix caching we typically see sub-100ms added overhead in well-architected networks.
05:34 Marcus Holt: sub-100ms is acceptable. how about burst capacity? we have seasonal spikes where 10% of tenants spike at once.
05:47 Sofia Martinez: for that we recommend Dedicated with burst pools — you reserve baseline throughput and allow a configurable burst bucket that uses pooled capacity. There's also graceful fallback to hosted smaller models if capacity is constrained.
06:01 Asha Singh: fallback to smaller models worries us for quality. we need deterministic outputs for legal docs.
06:10 Sofia Martinez: totally understood — you can pin a specific model version in Dedicated, and we can set rollout policies to avoid silent fallbacks for pinned routes. Private deployment is an option if you need absolute control.

08:40 Ethan Park: LangChain and LlamaIndex — we have maintained connectors and examples. Most teams either use our Redwood LLM wrapper in LangChain or instantiate the Redwood client directly and feed it into LlamaIndex. Do you use either today?
08:55 Asha Singh: prototyping with LangChain; LlamaIndex for doc retrieval tests. The friction point has been prompt templating and streaming partial responses into our UI.
09:10 Ethan Park: streaming is supported — you can stream token deltas directly into LangChain's stream handlers or wire our SDK stream to your socket. Note: some SDKs use SSE; if you run a proxy, ensure it supports chunked transfer / SSE passthrough. Some proxies buffer and break streams.
09:29 Marcus Holt: good to flag, our gateway currently buffers on response and would need a change.

11:05 Priya Nair: observability — we need per-request traces tied to our internal request IDs and token-level cost attribution. How does Redwood surface that?
11:18 Ethan Park: we emit correlation headers you can pass in (x-redwood-trace-id), and our console shows token breakdowns per request. You can also pull per-request logs via the API for a short retention window; for longer retention there's an add-on. We support OTEL hooks for spans so you can ingest into your existing tracing backend.
11:40 Priya Nair: what's the retention and sampling on the hosted plan?
11:45 Sofia Martinez: default is 30 days for request-level logs on hosted; Dedicated has configurable retention and you can ship logs to your S3 or SIEM. Private deployments put logs in your infra entirely.

14:00 Marcus Holt: quota enforcement — can we set per-route token caps and soft/ hard limits? we need throttling at model-level and per-tenant.
14:12 Ethan Park: yes — policies support per-API-key token quotas, rate limits (rps), and route-level caps. You can define soft limits with warning webhooks plus hard limits that return 429. There's also a usage webhook to sync with your billing system.
14:30 Marcus Holt: webhooks for warnings would be great. Does Redwood support immediate callbacks on soft-limit breach?
14:36 Ethan Park: yes, near-real-time with sub-second propagation for rate limit state in Dedicated; hosted depends on plan but typically sub-5s.

17:20 Asha Singh: security/compliance — Priya is pushing for SOC2 and encryption-at-rest keys managed by us, plus SSO. How does Redwood handle KMS?
17:33 Sofia Martinez: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own key) for model artifacts and logs; Private gives you full control. We integrate with common cloud KMS providers and HSM for on-prem. SSO via SAML/SCIM and RBAC are supported. We'll send the security pack.

20:02 Priya Nair: latency targets — our SLA needs 95th < 300ms for short-chat requests. Is that realistic with hosted?
20:12 Ethan Park: depends on model and sequence length. For small-chat-ish requests we can hit that in hosted from regional edge points for the majority, but Dedicated gives more predictable tail latencies. We'll run a micro-benchmark with your prompt set to confirm.

25:55 Marcus Holt: can you explain kv-cache/prefix caching? we do a lot of repeated context across sessions.
26:07 Ethan Park: KV cache is server-side recurrent cache of transformer KV states for long-running sessions; prefix caching re-uses embeddings and response fragments. It reduces token compute when you have repeated prefixes. Works best if you can provide stable conversation IDs from your side.
26:29 Asha Singh: so we need to pass conversation id through SDK?
26:33 Ethan Park: yes, pass conversation_id and optionally a cache_hint header to control TTL.

30:00 Priya Nair: about LlamaIndex connectors — any gotchas?
30:10 Ethan Park: larger issue is often how you chunk docs and the embedding model. We support multiple embedding models; we also recommend an embedding refresh cadence and caching. There's a sample LlamaIndex pipeline in the repo that handles vectorstore syncing and lazy reindexing.

34:40 Marcus Holt: failure modes — if Redwood is unreachable, we want deterministic local fallback. Any recommended patterns?
34:52 Ethan Park: typical is a local degraded model or earlier embedding snapshot. Another pattern is pre-warmed cache for common responses and stale-while-revalidate. For critical flows you can run Private or Dedicated in a VPC with peered networks so network failure surface area is minimized.

40:00 Priya Nair: pricing — Sofia?
40:06 Sofia Martinez: quick notes: hosted per-token + embedding units; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and burst bucket pricing; Private is enterprise pricing with license + support. We'll send a dedicated pricing sheet and a comparison matrix.

46:20 Marcus Holt: who owns the SDKs? open source? versioning?
46:28 Ethan Park: SDKs are OSS with pinned release branches; we publish breaking changes in the changelog and keep long-term support branches for major customers. We also provide sample infra terraform modules for Dedicated and Private deployments.

52:10 Asha Singh: final — do you have examples of rate-limit headers and webhook payloads?
52:18 Ethan Park: yes, we'll attach sample responses and a webhook payload schema in the follow-up.

58:00 Sofia Martinez: recap: redwood to share pricing + security pack + webhook samples, ethan to run bench, lyra to share prompts and traffic histogram, and we'll reconvene after bench results.
58:20 Priya Nair: sounds good. thanks all.
58:30 Sofia Martinez: thanks, talk soon. bye.

End of transcript.
